Reference-panel validation: supplementary tables

Table S1a. Panel checks and agreement with PRS-CS's published panels

Genome-wide PRS-LDmix panels (chromosomes 1–22, HapMap3 SNPs) built from the 33KG reference panel for five superpopulations, at both block layouts. Chromosomes passing: every panel lists the same SNPs and alleles in the same order, and every block's LD matrix is finite, symmetric, has a unit diagonal and |r| ≤ 1, and is positive definite. Agreement: correlation and root-mean-square difference between our within-block r and that of PRS-CS's published 1000 Genomes panel for the matching population, over SNP pairs in the same block in both panels, after aligning alleles; median and range over the 22 chromosomes. The 33KG reference panel includes the 1000 Genomes samples, and its AMR and SAS populations are the 1000 Genomes populations of those superpopulations, so the samples behind the two panels largely overlap: the comparison checks that the panels are built correctly, not that they replicate in independent samples.

Table S1b. Reference individuals and LD features by superpopulation

Fixed 250 kb panels. Each statistic is computed per chromosome and then averaged over chromosomes, weighted by SNP count. Mean r2, adjacent SNPs: the mean squared correlation between consecutive SNPs in the same block (pairs that span a block boundary are excluded). MAF, per-chromosome median: the median minor allele frequency of each chromosome, so not the genome-wide median. MAF < 0.05: the share of SNPs below 0.05. AFR shows the weaker short-range LD expected of African-ancestry populations.
